description: This exam certifies CEFR level A1 in Tagalog: you can interact in a simple way about yourself, your family, and your immediate needs — greeting people politely, introducing yourself, counting and telling time, ordering food, asking prices and directions, describing your daily routine in past, present, and future, and asking basic questions. It draws on all ten units, with emphasis on the ang/ng/sa marker system, the pronoun sets, and verb aspect.

questions.prompt: It's 7 p.m. and you meet your friend's grandfather. What do you say?
questions.explain: Gabi is evening/night, and po adds the politeness an elder expects.

questions.prompt: A teacher asks if you did your homework. The polite 'yes' is:
questions.explain: Opo is the polite form of oo, used with teachers, elders, and strangers.

questions.prompt: Ako ___ Miguel. Taga-Cebu ako. (I am Miguel.)
questions.explain: A person's name always takes the marker si after ako: Ako si Miguel.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explain: Ka is the 'you' that follows another word and can never start a sentence: Kumusta ka?

questions.tl: Magandang umaga po! Kumusta po kayo? — Mabuti naman. Ikaw?
questions.prompt: What is happening in this exchange?
choices: Two people say goodbye at night.
Someone greets an elder in the morning and asks how they are.
questions.explain: Magandang umaga is the morning greeting; po and kayo show respect; Kumusta and Mabuti naman are the how-are-you exchange.

questions.prompt: You and your friends (not the listener) are students. 'We are students' is:
questions.explain: Kami excludes the listener; tayo would include them.

questions.prompt: Count on: pito, walo, siyam, ___ (7, 8, 9, 10)
questions.explain: Sampu is ten in the native number set.

questions.prompt: Anong oras na? It's 2:30 in the afternoon. Which answer is right?
questions.explain: Alas-dos y medya = 2:30, and ng hapon places it in the afternoon.

questions.tl: Ilang taon ka na? — Dalawampu't limang taon na po ako.
questions.prompt: How old is the speaker?
questions.explain: Dalawampu't lima = twenty-five: dalawampu (20) + 't + lima (5).

questions.prompt: You didn't catch what someone said. What do you say?
choices: Pakiulit po, hindi ko po maintindihan.
questions.explain: Pakiulit asks them to repeat, and hindi ko maintindihan says you didn't understand.

questions.prompt: Estudyante ___ Ana at Liza. (Ana AND Liza are students — plural name marker)
questions.explain: Two or more names take sina instead of si.

questions.prompt: May kotse ka ba? You don't have one. The correct answer is:
questions.explain: May-questions are answered with mayroon or wala — never hindi.

questions.prompt: Your friend is holding a photo you can't see. You ask:
questions.explain: Iyan points at something near the listener; ito is near you, iyon is far from both.

questions.prompt: This is my mom. She is kind.
questions.answer: Ito ang nanay ko. Mabait siya.
accept: Ito ang nanay ko. Mabait siya
Ito po ang nanay ko. Mabait po siya
questions.explain: Ito introduces her, ko marks 'my', and Mabait siya needs no word for 'is'.

questions.prompt: Gusto ko ___ kape. (I want coffee.)
questions.explain: The thing wanted after gusto takes the marker ng: gusto ko ng kape.

questions.prompt: Which is correct for 'I like adobo'?
questions.explain: Gusto takes the ng-form pronoun ko; gusto ako would mean someone likes YOU.

questions.tl: Ano po ang gusto ninyo? — Isang sinigang po at kanin. Iyon lang po.
questions.prompt: What does the customer order?
questions.explain: Isang sinigang at kanin = one sinigang and rice; iyon lang po closes the order.

questions.prompt: May I have some water, please.
questions.explain: Pahingi po ng + noun is the polite set phrase for requesting something.

questions.prompt: 'Cold water' — which is correct?
questions.explain: Malamig ends in a consonant other than n, so the linker is the separate word na: malamig na tubig.

questions.prompt: Bago ang ___ sapatos ko. (My shoes — plural — are new.)
questions.explain: Mga before the noun makes it plural: ang mga sapatos ko = my shoes.

questions.prompt: What color is a ripe banana?
questions.explain: Dilaw is yellow. Pula is red, itim black, asul blue.

questions.tl: Maliit na itim na bag ang bag ko, at may pulang susi sa loob.
questions.prompt: Which bag is the speaker's?
choices: A big blue bag with a black key
A small black bag with a red key inside
A small red bag with keys outside
A big black bag with no keys
questions.explain: Maliit na itim na bag = small black bag; may pulang susi sa loob = there's a red key inside.

questions.prompt: ___ kusina si Nanay. (Mom is IN the kitchen.)
questions.explain: Nasa + place states location: Nasa kusina si Nanay.

questions.prompt: How do you ask where the bathroom is?
questions.explain: Nasaan asks the current location of a thing; saan pairs with action verbs like pupunta.

questions.prompt: Where are you going? — I'm going to the market.
questions.answer: Saan ka pupunta? — Pupunta ako sa palengke.
accept: Saan ka pupunta? Pupunta ako sa palengke
Saan po kayo pupunta? Pupunta po ako sa palengke
questions.explain: Saan (movement) + pupunta; the destination takes the marker sa.

questions.prompt: The market is beside the church. Which is correct?
choices: Nasa tabi ng simbahan ang palengke.
Nasa tabi sa simbahan ng palengke.
questions.explain: Position phrases run nasa + tabi + ng + landmark: nasa tabi ng simbahan = beside the church.

questions.prompt: Kumakain sila. What does this mean?
questions.explain: The repeated syllable with -um- still inside (kuMAkain) is the incompleted aspect: they are eating.

questions.prompt: 'I will drink coffee later' — ___ ako ng kape mamaya.
questions.explain: Contemplated -um- forms drop -um- and repeat the first syllable: inom → iinom.

questions.prompt: 'Mom cooked sinigang yesterday' — ___ si Nanay ng sinigang kahapon.
questions.explain: Kahapon demands the completed aspect, and mag- becomes nag-: nagluto.

questions.tl: Gumising ako nang alas-sais, naligo, kumain ng almusal, tapos pumunta sa trabaho.
questions.prompt: What is the speaker describing?
choices: What they are doing right now
questions.explain: Every verb is in the completed aspect (gumising, naligo, kumain, pumunta) — a finished sequence, told in order with tapos.

questions.prompt: Nagtatrabaho ang ate ko sa ospital. Umuuwi siya nang alas-otso ng gabi.
questions.answer: My older sister works at the hospital. She comes home at eight in the evening.
accept: My older sister works at the hospital. She comes home at eight in the evening
My big sister works at a hospital and goes home at 8 pm
My older sister works in the hospital. She goes home at eight at night
questions.explain: Both verbs are incompleted — habitual actions: nagtatrabaho (works), umuuwi (comes home).

questions.prompt: How do you ask the price of the mangoes?
questions.explain: Magkano asks price; ilan would ask how many, nasaan where, alin which one.

questions.tl: Magkano po lahat? — Sandaang piso po. — Heto po ang bayad. May sukli po ba ako?
questions.prompt: What is the total, and what does the buyer ask?
choices: Fifty pesos; where the store is
One hundred pesos; whether they get change
Twenty pesos; whether there's a discount
One hundred pesos; what time it is
questions.explain: Sandaang piso = 100 pesos; May sukli po ba ako? asks 'do I get change?'

questions.prompt: I will buy one kilo of tomatoes tomorrow.
questions.answer: Bibili ako ng isang kilo ng kamatis bukas.
accept: Bibili ako ng isang kilo ng kamatis bukas
Bukas, bibili ako ng isang kilo ng kamatis
Bibili ako bukas ng isang kilo ng kamatis
questions.explain: Bukas requires the contemplated bibili (no -um-), and the quantity chains as isang kilo ng kamatis.

questions.prompt: Which pairing is correct?
questions.explain: Ngayon (now) takes the incompleted umuulan. Kahapon/noong need completed umulan; bukas needs contemplated uulan.

questions.prompt: When did you arrive? — Last Saturday.
accept: Kailan po kayo dumating? Noong Sabado po
questions.explain: Kailan asks when; a past day takes noong (noong Sabado), while a future day would take sa.

questions.prompt: Bakit ka malungkot? — Kasi umuulan at may bagyo raw bukas.
questions.answer: Why are you sad? — Because it's raining and they say there's a typhoon tomorrow.
accept: Why are you sad? Because it's raining and they say there's a typhoon tomorrow
Why are you sad? Because it is raining and there is reportedly a typhoon tomorrow
Why are you sad? Because it's raining and there's supposedly a storm tomorrow
questions.explain: Bakit/kasi pair for why/because; umuulan is rain in progress; raw marks hearsay about tomorrow's typhoon.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses ang, ng, and sa all correctly?
choices: Bumili ang Lola sa saging ng palengke.
Bumili ng Lola ang saging sa palengke.
Bumili si Lola ng saging sa palengke.
Bumili sa Lola ng saging ang palengke.
questions.explain: Si Lola is the doer (a name takes si), ng saging marks what was bought, sa palengke marks where — the complete A1 marker system.
